title: Equivalent randomized time criteria
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $L$ be a language of binary strings, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. The following are equivalent: for every binary string $x$, every run of length $T(|x|)$ halts, members $x\in L$ have probability at least $2/3$ of producing the one-bit output $1$, and nonmembers produce the one-bit output $0$ on every choice word of length $T(|x|)$; and the same conditions with the member probability bound written as $2/3\leq \Pr[\text{output }1]$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
$L$ is a language of binary strings
